persona.name: Demo user
persona.description: A synthetic but internally consistent decision history for a person who is risk-averse and family-anchored, deliberates before committing, and becomes noticeably more willing to act when the upside is unusually large and family is not disturbed. It exists so the pipeline can be exercised end to end; it is not a real person and is not modelled on one.
designed_signals: Declines relocation and high-uncertainty opportunities when family is affected.
Accepts career growth readily when it does not disturb family proximity.
Becomes risk-tolerant only when the reward is exceptional - this is the interaction the reward-modulated risk tolerance term should recover.
Prefers deferring and researching when the picture is unclear and there is no deadline.
A late shift in 2025-2026 towards accepting more career risk, so preference-drift handling is exercised.

decisions.situation: A well-known consultancy in Bengaluru offered me a role paying about 60% more than my current salary. It would mean moving away from my parents, who I currently live with and help look after.
decisions.reason: The money was good but I could not justify leaving my parents on their own right now. My current job is stable and I am not unhappy in it.
decisions.outcome: Stayed. Got a small raise six months later.

decisions.situation: My manager offered me the lead role on a new internal project. More responsibility and visibility, no change to location or hours.
options: Decline and stay on my current work
decisions.reason: Real growth with no downside I could see. Nothing about my life outside work had to change.

decisions.situation: A friend asked me to put a substantial part of my savings into his early-stage venture. He was confident but the business had no revenue and no other investors yet.
options: Invest a large part of my savings
decisions.reason: Unproven business, no revenue, and it was money I could not afford to lose. Saying no was awkward with a friend but I could not gamble savings on it.
decisions.outcome: The venture shut down 18 months later.

decisions.situation: I could put my annual bonus into an index fund or leave it in a fixed deposit. The fund had better expected returns but could fall in any given year.
options: Put it in the index fund
Keep it in the fixed deposit
decisions.decision: Keep it in the fixed deposit
decisions.reason: I wanted to know exactly what the number would be. I compared both for weeks and still could not stomach the possibility of it going down.

decisions.situation: A part-time evening certification in data engineering. It would cost money and about ten hours a week for eight months, but it would clearly help my career in the long run.
decisions.reason: Hard work but it pays off over years and I could do it without changing anything else about my life.

decisions.situation: A recruiter approached me about a role at a one-year-old startup in Pune. About 40% more money, but early stage and I would have to move.
options: Accept the startup offer in Pune
decisions.reason: One year old with no clear runway, and relocation again. Too much uncertainty stacked on top of moving away from family.

decisions.situation: My team asked whether I wanted to move to a client-facing role. Same city, same pay, quite different day-to-day work and a lot more unpredictability in my schedule.
decisions.reason: I did not know enough about what the schedule would actually look like and nobody could tell me clearly. I would rather keep the predictable version.

decisions.situation: I found a flat closer to my office that would cut my commute by an hour a day, but it was 20% more expensive and I would be further from my parents.
options: Move to the flat near the office
decisions.reason: The commute is tiring but being fifteen minutes from my parents matters more to me than an hour a day.

decisions.situation: Offered a two-week unpaid research collaboration abroad. Excellent for my profile, cost me leave and some money, family fine with it because it was short.
decisions.reason: Short enough that nothing at home was disrupted, and the long-term value to my work was obvious.

decisions.situation: A colleague suggested I quit and go freelance. Potentially much more money and complete control over my time, but no guaranteed income at all.
decisions.reason: The freedom appealed to me more than I expected but I could not accept months with no guaranteed income while I support people at home.

decisions.situation: My insurance renewal came up with a cheaper provider I had not heard of, versus my existing one which costs more.
decisions.reason: I read the reviews for a long time and the savings were not worth an unknown company when it comes to a claim.

decisions.situation: An acquaintance offered me a place in a cryptocurrency trading pool with very high advertised returns and no clear explanation of how it worked.
decisions.reason: Nobody could explain to me how the returns were generated. That was enough.

decisions.situation: A promotion to senior analyst was offered, with a 25% raise and significantly longer hours during quarter ends.
decisions.reason: The extra hours are only a few weeks a year, the money is real, and it is the obvious next step. Nothing about where I live changes.

decisions.situation: A multinational offered me a role in Singapore at roughly three times my current salary, with relocation support and a five-year contract. My parents were healthy and my sister had moved back to live with them.
decisions.reason: This was different. Three times the money changes what I can do for my family long term, my sister is with our parents now, and the company has been around for decades. I researched it for two months before saying yes.

decisions.situation: In Singapore I could rent a small flat close to the office or a larger one further out for the same money.
options: Take the small flat near the office
Take the larger flat further out
decisions.decision: Take the small flat near the office
decisions.reason: Less commuting and less hassle while I settle in. I did not need the space.

decisions.situation: An internal transfer to a newly formed team was available. Interesting work but the team had existed for three months and there was talk that it might be restructured.
decisions.reason: I had only just arrived in a new country. Adding an unstable team on top of that was more change than I wanted at once.

decisions.situation: My employer offered stock options in place of part of my cash bonus. Higher expected value, but the value depends on the share price in four years.
decisions.reason: I am sending money home every month. I cannot make that depend on a share price four years out.

decisions.situation: A recruiter offered a role at a competitor with a 15% raise but a reputation for very long hours and high turnover.
decisions.reason: Fifteen percent does not buy back my evenings, and the churn there told me something.

decisions.situation: I was asked to present at a large industry conference. Good exposure but I find public speaking stressful and it required a lot of preparation.
decisions.reason: Uncomfortable but it builds something that lasts, and I had three months to prepare properly.

decisions.situation: My parents needed help with a large medical expense. I could pay it from savings immediately or take a low-interest loan and keep my savings buffer intact.
decisions.reason: I was not going to have this hanging over the family as a debt. The buffer can be rebuilt.

decisions.situation: A recruiter offered a fully remote role at similar pay that would let me move back to be near my parents.
options: Take the remote role and move back
decisions.decision: Take the remote role and move back
decisions.reason: Same money, and it puts me back near my parents after the health scare. There was nothing to weigh.

decisions.situation: With the money saved in Singapore I could buy a flat outright or keep renting and invest the difference in the market.
decisions.reason: Owning it outright means nobody can take it away and there is no monthly uncertainty. I know the market probably returns more on paper.

decisions.situation: An old colleague asked me to join his consultancy as a partner. Uncapped upside, but I would take a 50% pay cut for the first year with no guarantee it works.
decisions.reason: A year at half pay right after buying a flat is not something I can carry, however good the upside looks.

decisions.situation: A short online course on machine learning for finance, moderate cost, evenings and weekends for three months.
decisions.reason: Cheap relative to what it opens up later. I would rather build the skill before I need it.

decisions.situation: A vendor offered me a personal gift to influence which supplier my team selected. Nobody would have known.
decisions.reason: That is not a thing I do, regardless of whether anyone would find out.

decisions.situation: My employer restructured and offered either a voluntary exit package worth eight months of salary, or a transfer to a different function I had no experience in.
decisions.reason: Eight months of money runs out. A job does not. I would rather learn something new than be looking for work.

decisions.situation: Friends were pressuring me to join an expensive group holiday. I did not really want to go and it would have cost a month of savings.
decisions.reason: I did not want to go and the cost was hard to justify. They were annoyed but that passed.

decisions.situation: I was offered the chance to lead a high-visibility project with a real chance of public failure, but a large bonus and a likely promotion if it worked.
decisions.reason: I have more of a cushion now than I used to. The upside is large and even if it fails I keep my job.
decisions.outcome: Took it. Delivered late but delivered.

decisions.situation: A small allocation of my portfolio into higher-risk equity, roughly 10% of what I hold, with the rest staying conservative.
decisions.reason: Ten percent is an amount I can lose entirely without it changing anything. That is a different question from betting savings.

decisions.situation: A former manager offered me a role at a Series B startup, 80% more money, in my own city, no relocation. The company had four years of history and named investors.
decisions.reason: Four years in with real investors is not the same as a one-year-old company. No relocation, big raise, and I know the person I would report to. I still took six weeks to decide.

decisions.situation: The new company offered to move me onto a mostly equity compensation package with much higher potential value.
decisions.reason: I took the job risk already. I am not going to take the compensation risk on top of it.

decisions.situation: I had to decide whether to hire quickly from a shortlist I was not fully convinced by, or keep the role open and keep searching while my team was short-staffed.
decisions.reason: A wrong hire costs a year. Being short-staffed for another month is annoying but recoverable.

decisions.situation: An urgent decision: a supplier offered a large discount if I committed by the end of the day, with no time to check their references.
options: Let the discount go and check properly
decisions.decision: Let the discount go and check properly
decisions.reason: Anything that needs my signature today and will not survive two days of checking is telling me something.

decisions.situation: I was invited to co-found a side venture with two people I respect. It would take most of my evenings and weekends for at least a year, with genuine long-term upside and no immediate income.
options: Decline and stay focused on my job
decisions.decision: Decline and stay focused on my job
decisions.reason: I had just started somewhere new. Doing both badly is worse than doing one well.

decisions.situation: My company offered a sabbatical option: three months unpaid to travel or study, with my role held open.
decisions.reason: Three months without income while I am still new in the role. Maybe in a few years.

decisions.situation: A competitor offered me roughly double my current salary to move to Dubai on a three-year contract. Established company, but it would mean leaving my parents again, and my sister has since moved abroad.
decisions.reason: Double is a lot of money. But there is nobody else near my parents now, and I have been here two years. It was closer than I expected.

decisions.situation: An internal opening to lead a small team in the same office, modest raise, more management and less hands-on technical work.
decisions.reason: It is the direction I want long term and nothing else in my life has to change to do it.

facts.content: Lives in the same city as their parents and is the primary person available to help them.
Sends money home monthly and owns their flat outright with no mortgage.
Works in data and analytics; currently a team lead at a Series B company.
